principle_correct.critique: The answer names the principle. It says strong repulsion U stops two electrons from sharing a site, and that this makes the half-filled crystal an insulator. It ties the U=0 case to band theory and the U=8 case to La2CuO4. It also says the leftover hopping makes neighboring spins point opposite ways, which explains the antiferromagnetism. It says hole doping brings superconductivity. All of this is correct at the level of the toy model. It does not mention that the real material is a charge-transfer insulator, but the task framed it as a Mott insulator, so that is not a fault.
